common.configError: Your old configuration could not be converted, so Joulenap started with no devices and no routes. Don't save anything until it's fixed. {{reason}}

auth.sessionExpired: Your session expired. Please sign in again.
auth.signInSubtitle: Enter your credentials to manage the scheduler.
auth.registerSubtitle: No account configured. Create the administration credentials to get started.
auth.timezoneHint: Detected from your browser. The backup schedule runs in this timezone — you can change it later under Settings.

errors.userShort: The username must be at least 3 characters.

dashboard.scheduleCustom: Custom schedule set in config.yaml ({{cron}}) — edit it there to change.
dashboard.guestsError: Couldn't refresh the guest list — showing the last known guests.
dashboard.noGuests: No guests found on this node.
dashboard.noGuestsSelected: Select at least one guest, or switch to General backup — Selective mode with no guests backs up nothing.
dashboard.runsError: Couldn't load the run history — retrying.
dashboard.noTaskLog: No task output yet — appears here live during backup, GC and verify.

confirm.offMsg: The PBS will be shut down now. The scheduler will wake it automatically for the next scheduled backup.
confirm.gcNote: If the PBS is sleeping, it is woken before the GC.
confirm.verifyNote: Verifies the datastore snapshots. If the PBS is sleeping, it is woken.
confirm.powerOffAfter: Power off the PBS when finished
confirm.onNote: {{pbs}} is sleeping. Joulenap sends the Wake-on-LAN packet and shows it as on in the backup map. With no active jobs it stays on until you power it off from here.
confirm.stopRouteMsg: The task running on the server is stopped with the run, and anything still queued behind it does not start. Data already written is kept; the run is recorded as aborted.

dashboard.powerLocked: A run is using this server — power is locked until it finishes
dashboard.noRoutes: No routes yet — create one to start backing up.

routeModal.deleteBody: "{{name}}" will stop running and disappear from the backup map. Snapshots already on the PBS are not touched, and its past runs stay in the history.
routeModal.name: Route name
routeModal.sourcesHelp: Multiple PVEs in one route = a single wake→backup→power-off cycle. A PBS source creates a sync route.
routeModal.targetHelp: Woken via WoL and powered back off when the route finishes.
routeModal.targetIsSource: Already the target of this route
routeModal.onWakeHelp: No sources: the route only wakes the PBS. External = PVE/PBS run the jobs they schedule themselves (watch timeouts are in Settings). Verify = verifies the datastore snapshots.
routeModal.previewExternal: wake → watch PVE/PBS schedules → power off
routeModal.previewVerify: wake → verify the datastore → power off
routeModal.guestsHelp: In “All” mode, new guests are included in the backup automatically.
routeModal.syncHelp: Both PBS are woken; each is powered back off once its tasks are done.
routeModal.retentionOverlap: Same target and overlapping guests as {{routes}}, but a different retention. PBS prunes per backup group, so whichever route runs last decides how many snapshots survive.
routeModal.notifyLabel: Send notifications for this route (success and failure)
routeModal.notifyHelp: Turn this off to exclude this route from notifications — other routes are unaffected. Channels are configured in Settings → Notifications.
routeModal.minFreeHelp: Below this threshold the route does not start. 0 = off
routeModal.gc: Run garbage collection when this route finishes
routeModal.errSyncSingle: A sync route has a single PBS source.
routeModal.errNoStorage: {{pve}} has no storage for {{pbs}}. Add it in Datacenter → Storage on that PVE, then re-run the setup for it.
routeModal.errExternalUnmanaged: {{pbs}} is always on, so there is nothing for an External route to wake or power off.
routeModal.errNoDay: Pick at least one day, or disable the route instead.
routeModal.errNoGuests: No guest is selected, so this route would back up nothing.
routeModal.errDuplicate: A route with that name already exists.

pve.title: Add Proxmox VE
pve.storagesFound: PBS storages found in this PVE's configuration
pve.noStorages: No PBS storage found in this PVE. Add the storage in PVE and run this again, or add a PBS on its own from Settings → Devices.
pve.newStorage: New — not yet registered in Joulenap · fingerprint captured
pve.storagesHelp: An already-registered storage is linked automatically, with no extra steps.
pve.oneAtATime: One new PBS is configured per run — add the others from Settings → Devices → + Add.
pve.pbsReachable: {{host}} reachable · fingerprint pinned from the storage config
pve.readyBody: No route is configured yet: create one from “+ New route” on the homepage — sources, time, guests and retention are chosen there.

pbs.title: Add Proxmox Backup Server
pbs.orphan: No registered PVE sends backups to {{id}}: Backup routes to it are unavailable until you add the storage in Proxmox VE, then open Settings → Devices → that PVE → Edit and press “Re-read from Proxmox”. Sync, Verify and External routes work right away.

tokenExists.title: That token name is already taken
tokenExists.message: An API token with the name Joulenap uses already exists on this server. Its secret is only shown when it is created, so Joulenap cannot reuse it — it can only replace it. Anything else still using that token stops working immediately, which on a Proxmox host usually means the backup-server storage entry, and every backup through it. Replace it only if you know nothing else uses it.
tokenExists.usedByDevice: “{{id}}” in Joulenap already authenticates to this server — replacing the token breaks it.
tokenExists.usedByStorage: Storage “{{storage}}” on “{{pve}}” authenticates to this server with it, so backups through that storage would start failing.

cred.pveHelp: Root credentials are used only now to create the dedicated token — they are never stored.
cred.pbsHelp: Used only to create the dedicated token, grant it what Sync routes need and install the SSH key — never stored.
cred.pbsInPveHelp: The PBS is a different machine from the PVE: it needs its own credentials. Root is used only now to create the token and install the SSH key — never stored.
cred.fingerprintPinned: This fingerprint is pinned — connections are rejected if it changes.

field.name: Name
field.nameHelp: The name shown everywhere in Joulenap. Lower-case letters, digits, . _ and -

wake.macHelp: Detected via ARP while the PBS is powered on. If it is off, type it in.
wake.macDetected: ✓ Detected via ARP — the PBS is on right now.
wake.wolSent: ✓ Magic packet sent to {{broadcast}} — watch whether the box wakes.
wake.biosWarning: Enable Wake-on-LAN in the PBS BIOS and arm it in the OS (ethtool -s <nic> wol g, persistent) — Joulenap cannot do this remotely.
wake.ifaceHint: Interface Joulenap sends the Wake-on-LAN packet from; once the PBS host is set the packet is scoped to its subnet, not the whole network.

power.managedHint: Turn this off for an always-on PBS (a VM, or a cloud-hosted one): Joulenap only schedules against it, and the wake-up and power-off steps are skipped.

ssh.title: SSH key for power-off
ssh.reused: Reusing the key Joulenap already has — generating a new one would break power-off on the boxes that already trust this one.
ssh.autoInstall: Install automatically with the (transient) root credentials
ssh.hostKeyWhy: Confirm the PBS host key before the root password is sent; it is then stored in known_hosts.
ssh.manualHint: Add the line below to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys on the PBS, then mark as installed.

report.pbsConfigured: {{id}} · token created · SSH ok · MAC saved
report.sshInstalled: SSH key installed · host key stored
report.sshManual: SSH key ready — paste the line above into the PBS's authorized_keys
report.unmanaged: Always-on PBS: Joulenap never wakes or powers it off

err.idPattern: Use lower-case letters, digits, dots, underscores or dashes, starting with a letter or digit.
err.idTaken: “{{id}}” is already taken by another device.
err.passwordRequired: A password is required for transient-root setup.
err.tokenRequired: Both the token ID and its secret are required.
err.installNeedsRoot: Installing the key automatically needs the root credentials. Switch to transient root, or turn the toggle off and paste the line yourself.
err.hostKeyNotTrusted: Confirm the PBS host key first — the root password is only sent over a connection whose host key you have checked.
err.pbsUnreachable: PBS is not reachable at that host and port. Check it is powered on and the address is correct, then try again.
err.macNotDetected: Couldn't auto-detect the MAC address — enter it manually.
err.alreadyRegistered: This address is already registered as “{{id}}”. Edit that device instead — adding it again would replace its API token and leave the original unable to connect.

localization.timezoneHint: Timezone the backup schedule is interpreted in. Leave on Automatic to use the TZ environment variable, falling back to UTC.

account.title: Account
account.subtitle: The sign-in for this web interface

notifications.customDesc: One URL per line — any Apprise service or plain webhook.
notifications.saveFirst: Save your changes before sending a test.
notifications.eventsHint: The per-route filter lives in the route editor

integrations.title: API key
integrations.subtitle: Protects /api/dashboard and /metrics · read-only
integrations.keyShownOnce: The full key is shown only right after generation. Regenerating invalidates the previous one.
integrations.copyFailed: Couldn't copy automatically — select the text and copy it manually.
integrations.snippetHint: Paste it into your dashboard's config, indentation intact. With routes the response is a list — one entry per route and one per backup server.
integrations.regenerateConfirmBody: The current key will stop working immediately. Any dashboard using it must be updated with the new key.
integrations.disableConfirmBody: The endpoint will return 403 and any dashboard widget using it will stop working.
integrations.keyHidden: A key is configured — the full value is shown only right after generation.
integrations.promMetricsHint: Exposed series. With routes, every per-route and per-PBS metric carries the label that says which one — a query without it sums unrelated devices.
integrations.snippetIndexNote:
# routes.0 / pbss.0 are the FIRST configured route and backup server; bump the
# index (routes.1, pbss.1, ...) for the others, or add a second widget.
integrations.snippetQueryAuth: (or API Key (Query), param "key", if your version lacks header auth:
integrations.snippetIndexHint: Index into the lists, e.g. routes.0.next_run / pbss.0.datastore_used_pct.
integrations.snippetCors: # No CORS? set useProxy: true, or fall back to {{url}}

advanced.historyDaysHint: Run history and activity-log rows older than this are pruned daily so the database can't grow without bound. 0 keeps everything forever.
advanced.restartHint: ⚠️ The port and the two session settings only take effect after the container is restarted.
advanced.portHint: Port the app listens on inside the container. Changing it also means changing the port mapping of your container.
advanced.httpsOnlyHint: Enable when Joulenap is served over HTTPS or behind a TLS-terminating proxy. Leaving it on over plain HTTP will lock you out of signing in.
advanced.yamlSubtitle: The whole configuration, exactly as it is stored. Everything the forms don't cover lives here.
advanced.yamlHint: Secrets are shown as ***REDACTED*** — leave them as-is to keep the stored value, or type a new one to replace it. A key you delete keeps its current value; the document is validated before anything is written.
advanced.copyFailed: Couldn't copy automatically — select the text and copy it manually.
advanced.schedulerHint: Global switch: with it off no route starts from its schedule, though manual runs still work. A persistent banner appears below the header while it is off.
advanced.updateCheck: Check once a day whether a newer release exists
advanced.updateCheckHint: Opt-in: without it, Joulenap makes no outbound internet calls.
advanced.exportHint: Export downloads what is in the editor. Secrets are redacted in it, so it is a readable copy for reference — not a restorable backup.

devices.removeBody: The device is removed from the configuration. Nothing is deleted on the machine itself, and the run history keeps its records.
devices.guardBody_one: {{id}} is used by 1 route. Change or delete it first — removing the device would break it.
devices.guardBody_other: {{id}} is used by {{count}} routes. Change or delete them first — removing the device would break them.
devices.syncGrantHint: A Sync route needs the /remote roles on this box’s token. Tokens created by Joulenap 1.0 already have them; one added by hand, or by an older version, does not — and PBS only accepts the grant from a root login.
devices.syncGrantCreds: Root credentials are used only for this grant and are never stored.
devices.secretHelp: Leave it untouched to keep the stored secret; clear the field to remove it.
devices.storagesEmpty: No backup server is mapped to a storage on this PVE yet, so no backup route can target one.
devices.storagesHint: Which PVE storage points at which backup server. Read from the PVE's own storage configuration — add the storage in Proxmox VE, then re-read it here.
devices.managedPowerHint: Off for an always-on or cloud-hosted backup server: Joulenap schedules routes against it but never wakes it and never shuts it down.
devices.poweroffWaitHint: A running PBS task is given this long to finish, so a shutdown never cuts one off. 0 powers off immediately.
devices.firstTaskWaitHint: How long to wait for the first task to appear after wake-up.
devices.idleWaitHint: Power off after this many seconds with no active task.
devices.errPort: The port must be between 1 and 65535.
devices.errPowerField: Required while Joulenap manages this box's power.
